newsitem.title: USA: Compaq cuts prices of certain business PCs.
newsitem.headline: Compaq cuts prices of certain business PCs.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. Tuesday cut prices on several business desktop personal computers by up to 23 percent and slashed prices on related desktop options, including memory and the Compaq Scanner Keyboard, by up to 53 percent.
The cuts affect certain Compaq ProLinea and Deskpro desktop PC models, many of which feature fast Pentium processors and large hard drives.

For example, the Compaq Deskpro 5150 Model 1200 now sells for $1,825, $330 less than before. The Compaq Scanner Keyboard, the first product to integrate paper-driven document scanning with a high-quality Windows 95-based keyboard, is now 8 percent cheaper at $299, it said.
Houston-based Compaq is the world's largest supplier of PCs, with worldwide sales of $14.8 billion in 1995.
Its stock fell 75 cents to $55.875 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
